title: Amazon AI Recruitment System
setup: Amazon built an AI system to help choose which job applicants to interview.
question: Which problem was discovered?
choices: It treated signs associated with women as a reason to rank applicants lower
It favored applicants who had attended a small group of famous universities
It rejected too many people who had taken time away from work
It regularly placed younger applicants above older ones
correct_choice: It treated signs associated with women as a reason to rank applicants lower
explanation: The system learned unfair patterns from past hiring records and ranked many women lower.
lesson: AI can inherit human biases, causing unfair discrimination.
original_description: Amazon stopped using a hiring system after finding evidence that it discriminated against women.

title: Genderify - Gender identification tool
setup: A website tried to guess a person's gender from their name and email address.
question: Why was the website shut down?
choices: Its guesses often relied on stereotypes and were frequently wrong
It stored people's email addresses without clearly telling them
It often failed when a person had a short name
It gave different answers depending on which web browser was used
correct_choice: Its guesses often relied on stereotypes and were frequently wrong
explanation: The tool made inaccurate and stereotyped guesses about people's gender.
lesson: AI tools can produce biased and unreliable results.
original_description: A tool that guessed gender from names and email addresses was closed after people exposed its bias and errors.

title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science
setup: Researchers checked hundreds of studies that used AI to make scientific predictions.
question: Which problem did they find?
choices: Many studies accidentally tested their AI with information it had already seen
Many studies did not say what kind of computer system they used
Many studies used too few examples to compare results fairly
Many studies relied on private information that other researchers could not check
correct_choice: Many studies accidentally tested their AI with information it had already seen
explanation: Many studies gave their AI an unfair advantage, making the reported results look better than they really were.
lesson: Poor experimental design can cause unreliable AI research.
original_description: Reviews across 17 fields found serious testing mistakes in 329 scientific papers that used AI.

title: COVID-19 Diagnosis and Triage Models
setup: Hundreds of AI systems were built to diagnose COVID-19 or decide which patients needed urgent care.
question: What did researchers discover?
choices: None of the reviewed systems were ready for patient care, and some could cause harm
The systems worked in large hospitals but not in small clinics
The systems found severe cases but missed most mild cases
The systems were accurate but too slow for emergency rooms
correct_choice: None of the reviewed systems were ready for patient care, and some could cause harm
explanation: Poor testing and unreliable results meant the systems could not safely be used with patients.
lesson: AI must be properly tested before real-world medical use.
original_description: Researchers reviewed hundreds of COVID-19 prediction systems and found that none were suitable for patient care.

title: COMPAS Recidivism Algorithm
setup: A court system used AI to predict who might commit another crime.
question: Which unfair pattern was reported?
choices: Black defendants were more often wrongly labeled as high risk
Scores changed depending on which judge requested them
Minor past offenses were treated like violent crimes
Predictions became less accurate when someone moved to another county
correct_choice: Black defendants were more often wrongly labeled as high risk
explanation: The system was more likely to wrongly label Black defendants as likely to commit another crime.
lesson: AI can perpetuate racial biases in justice systems.
original_description: An investigation found racial differences in the mistakes made by a court risk-scoring system.

title: Pennsylvania Child Welfare Screening Tool
setup: A child welfare agency used AI to help decide which families should be investigated.
question: Which problem was reported?
choices: Black children were sent for required investigations more often than other children
Rural families were flagged more often because records were incomplete
Children living with grandparents were given unusually high risk ratings
Families receiving public assistance were sometimes counted more than once
correct_choice: Black children were sent for required investigations more often than other children
explanation: The tool sent a disproportionate number of Black children for investigations.
lesson: AI can cause unfair targeting in sensitive social services.
original_description: A Pennsylvania screening tool disproportionately flagged Black children for required neglect investigations.

title: Oregon Child Welfare Screening Tool
setup: Oregon used AI to help decide which child welfare reports needed investigation.
question: What happened after concerns were raised about a similar tool?
choices: Oregon stopped using its tool about a month later
Oregon required two social workers to approve every suggestion
Oregon removed neighborhood and race information but kept the tool
Oregon delayed wider use while arranging an outside review
correct_choice: Oregon stopped using its tool about a month later
explanation: Oregon quickly stopped using its tool after concerns about a similar system became public.
lesson: Similar AI tools can replicate biases across regions.
original_description: Oregon ended use of its child welfare screening tool about a month after a report on a similar system.

title: U.S. Healthcare System Health Risk Prediction
setup: A healthcare system used AI to predict which patients needed the most care.
question: Which hidden problem did researchers find?
choices: Black patients were often much sicker than white patients given the same rating
Older patients received lower ratings because older records mattered less
Rural patients received higher ratings because travel costs counted as care
Patients with chronic pain received lower ratings when prescriptions were missing
correct_choice: Black patients were often much sicker than white patients given the same rating
explanation: The system used healthcare spending as a sign of need, which caused it to underestimate the needs of many Black patients.
lesson: AI can embed racial bias in healthcare predictions.
original_description: A widely used healthcare system gave equal ratings to Black and white patients even when the Black patients were considerably sicker.

title: Apple Card Credit Card
setup: A credit card used an automated system to decide how much money each customer could borrow.
question: Which problem caused complaints?
choices: Some women received far lower limits than men with similar finances
Self-employed people received lower limits despite strong credit histories
Longtime customers received higher limits than otherwise similar applicants
People in expensive neighborhoods received limits that ignored their income
correct_choice: Some women received far lower limits than men with similar finances
explanation: Customers reported large differences between limits offered to men and women with similar finances.
lesson: AI can perpetuate gender discrimination in finance.
original_description: Financial regulators investigated complaints that women received much lower Apple Card limits than men, including married couples with shared finances.

title: Inverness Automated Football Camera System
setup: An automated camera tried to follow the ball while filming a soccer match.
question: What did the camera follow by mistake?
choices: A bald assistant referee's head
The referee's brightly colored shirt
A white banner in the crowd
The ball's shadow on the field
correct_choice: A bald assistant referee's head
explanation: The camera repeatedly mistook a bald head for the ball and moved away from the action.
lesson: Computer vision can misinterpret similar visual features.
original_description: During a live soccer broadcast, an automated camera repeatedly followed an assistant referee's bald head instead of the ball.

title: Amazon Rekognition for US Congressmen
setup: A group tested a face-matching system using photos of lawmakers and police mugshots.
question: What happened in the test?
choices: It wrongly matched 28 lawmakers with people in the mugshot collection
It confused several lawmakers with other politicians who looked similar
It could not check lawmakers who wore glasses in their official photos
It made far more mistakes with older lawmakers than younger ones
correct_choice: It wrongly matched 28 lawmakers with people in the mugshot collection
explanation: The system falsely connected 28 members of Congress with criminal mugshots.
lesson: Facial recognition can produce false positives and bias.
original_description: A test of Amazon's face-matching system falsely matched 28 members of Congress with people in a mugshot database.

title: Amazon Rekognition for law enforcement
setup: Researchers tested a face-analysis system offered to police departments.
question: Which group did the system struggle with most?
choices: Women with darker skin
Older men with facial hair
Younger people of every skin tone
People shown on security-camera footage
correct_choice: Women with darker skin
explanation: The system made more gender-identification mistakes for darker-skinned women.
lesson: Facial recognition can be biased against gender and skin tone.
original_description: Tests found that Amazon's face-analysis system often identified darker-skinned women as men.

title: Zhejiang traffic facial recognition system
setup: Traffic cameras used face matching to identify people crossing streets illegally.
question: Which mistake actually happened?
choices: A woman's face on a bus advertisement was reported as a person crossing the street
A cyclist waiting at a red light was reported as a pedestrian
A person's reflection in a shop window was reported as a pedestrian
Someone behind a crossing barrier received a ticket
correct_choice: A woman's face on a bus advertisement was reported as a person crossing the street
explanation: The camera treated a large printed face on a moving bus as a real person.
lesson: AI can mistake images in complex environments.
original_description: A traffic camera mistakenly reported a woman's face on the side of a bus as someone crossing the street illegally.

title: Kneron tricking facial recognition terminals
setup: Researchers tested payment machines that approve purchases by recognizing a customer's face.
question: How were some machines fooled?
choices: A realistic three-dimensional mask was accepted as a real face
Special contact lenses made one customer look like another
A video on a phone was accepted without anyone present
Invisible light caused the machines to approve unknown faces
correct_choice: A realistic three-dimensional mask was accepted as a real face
explanation: Some payment machines accepted realistic masks instead of a real customer's face.
lesson: Facial recognition can be tricked by realistic disguises.
original_description: Researchers used realistic three-dimensional masks to fool face-based payment systems and make purchases.

title: Twitter smart cropping tool
setup: Twitter used AI to choose which part of a photo appeared in a preview.
question: Which concern did people find?
choices: The previews sometimes favored white faces over Black faces
The previews favored younger faces over older faces
The previews favored people looking directly at the camera
The previews left out wheelchair users in group photos
correct_choice: The previews sometimes favored white faces over Black faces
explanation: Public tests suggested the automatic previews were more likely to center white faces.
lesson: AI can reflect societal biases in image processing.
original_description: Twitter's automatic photo-cropping tool showed signs of racial bias in the faces it chose to display.

title: Depixelator tool
setup: An AI tool tried to create a clear face from a very blurry, blocky picture.
question: Which unfair pattern appeared?
choices: The finished faces often looked white, even when the original person did not
The finished faces looked younger and lost signs of age
The finished faces looked more masculine when the picture was very blurry
The finished faces copied features from famous people
correct_choice: The finished faces often looked white, even when the original person did not
explanation: When information was missing, the tool often filled in the face with white-looking features.
lesson: AI image generation can reflect racial biases in training data.
original_description: A tool for rebuilding clear faces from blocky images produced results that were heavily skewed toward white-looking people.

title: Google Photos tagging
setup: Google Photos used AI to automatically label people and objects in pictures.
question: Which offensive mistake occurred?
choices: It labeled photos of Black people as gorillas
It labeled guide dogs as wolves
It treated identical twins as the same person
It labeled bicycles with child seats as motorcycles
correct_choice: It labeled photos of Black people as gorillas
explanation: The photo system applied a deeply offensive animal label to pictures of Black people.
lesson: AI can produce harmful racial misclassifications.
original_description: Google Photos mistakenly labeled Black people in photographs as gorillas.

title: GenderShades evaluation of gender classification products
setup: Researchers tested systems that tried to identify a person's gender from a photo.
question: Which group had the most errors?
choices: Women with darker skin
Older adults of every skin tone
People shown in video rather than still photos
People wearing makeup or glasses
correct_choice: Women with darker skin
explanation: The systems were far less accurate for darker-skinned women than for lighter-skinned men.
lesson: AI gender classification can have racial and gender bias.
original_description: Tests of face-analysis services from Microsoft and IBM found frequent mistakes when analyzing darker-skinned women.

title: New Jersey Police Facial Recognition
setup: Police used a face-matching system to help identify a suspect.
question: What happened after a wrong match?
choices: An innocent Black man was jailed even though he was far from the crime
Police searched the home of someone who looked like the suspect's sibling
A witness changed their choice after seeing the computer's suggested person
An innocent driver was detained because of an old police photo
correct_choice: An innocent Black man was jailed even though he was far from the crime
explanation: A false match contributed to the arrest and jailing of an innocent man.
lesson: Facial recognition errors can cause serious legal harm.
original_description: New Jersey police jailed Nijeer Parks after a false face match, even though he was 30 miles away when the crime occurred.

title: Tesla's dilemma between a horse cart and a truck
setup: A car's display tried to identify a horse-drawn carriage on the road.
question: What did the display show?
choices: It switched between showing a truck and a person
It showed two bicycles moving together
It showed a person pulling a trailer
It showed roadwork equipment
correct_choice: It switched between showing a truck and a person
explanation: The car could not make sense of the unusual vehicle and kept changing its guess.
lesson: Computer vision can confuse unfamiliar objects in traffic.
original_description: A Tesla display confused a horse-drawn carriage with a truck and a person walking behind it.

title: Google's AI for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
setup: Clinics tested AI that examined eye photos for signs of diabetes-related disease.
question: What went wrong in real clinics?
choices: Poor-quality photos and internet delays made the system work worse than expected
It sent too many early cases for urgent treatment
It accepted photos from only one type of camera
Doctors often rejected correct results because the ratings were unclear
correct_choice: Poor-quality photos and internet delays made the system work worse than expected
explanation: Real clinics had blurry photos and unreliable internet, problems that were less common during controlled testing.
lesson: AI systems may fail when moved from lab to real world.
original_description: An AI eye-screening tool performed worse in clinics because it rejected poor-quality photos and relied on unreliable internet connections.

title: Google Flu Trends
setup: Google used search activity to estimate how many people had the flu.
question: Which prediction problem became well known?
choices: It greatly overestimated the number of flu cases
It noticed outbreaks too late because searches changed slowly
It confused allergy searches with flu searches
It predicted local outbreaks but missed the national pattern
correct_choice: It greatly overestimated the number of flu cases
explanation: Changes in what people searched for caused the system to predict far more flu cases than there actually were.
lesson: Forecasting models can be unreliable without proper validation.
original_description: Google's search-based flu tracker produced inaccurate estimates that were much too high.

title: Zillow iBuying algorithms
setup: A company used AI to predict home prices and buy houses automatically.
question: Which problem helped end the program?
choices: It paid too much for many homes and lost a large amount of money
Renovation costs were accurate, but the homes took too long to sell
It bought heavily in growing cities just as demand moved elsewhere
Its offers were so low that it could not buy enough homes
correct_choice: It paid too much for many homes and lost a large amount of money
explanation: Inaccurate price estimates caused the company to overpay for homes it could not resell profitably.
lesson: AI price predictions can lead to costly errors.
original_description: Zillow suffered major losses in its home-buying business after its price predictions were too high.

title: Tyndaris Robot Hedge Fund
setup: An investment company let an AI system choose how to trade its money.
question: Which outcome was reported?
choices: Large losses were followed by a lawsuit from an investor
The system accidentally made the same trade several times
The company blocked withdrawals after underestimating market risk
Delayed price information caused trades at the wrong time
correct_choice: Large losses were followed by a lawsuit from an investor
explanation: The AI-guided strategy lost a large amount of money and became the subject of a legal dispute.
lesson: Automated trading AI can cause financial risks and failures.
original_description: An automated investment system named K1 caused major losses that eventually led to a lawsuit.

title: Sentient Investment AI Hedge Fund
setup: An investment fund used AI to decide when to buy and sell.
question: What happened to the fund?
choices: It failed to make money and was closed
It stayed open but switched to a mix of people and AI
Trading fees erased the money it appeared to earn
A larger fund bought it after it repeatedly fell behind
correct_choice: It failed to make money and was closed
explanation: The AI strategy did not produce profits, and the fund closed in less than two years.
lesson: AI investment funds can fail despite initial promise.
original_description: An AI-run investment fund failed to make money and was closed in under two years.

title: JP Morgan's Deep Learning Model for FX Algos
setup: A bank used AI to decide how to buy and sell different currencies.
question: Why did the bank stop using it?
choices: The system had trouble making sense of the market information it received
It reacted too slowly when currency prices changed quickly
It made money but was too difficult for reviewers to understand
It depended on price information the bank could no longer access
correct_choice: The system had trouble making sense of the market information it received
explanation: The system was difficult to use because it did not interpret market information reliably.
lesson: Complex AI models may be unreliable in financial markets.
original_description: JPMorgan stopped using an AI currency-trading system because of problems interpreting information and managing its complexity.

title: Playground AI facial generation
setup: A woman used an AI photo editor to turn her headshot into a professional profile picture.
question: Which unexpected change did it make?
choices: It changed the Asian woman's face to look white
It made her look much younger and changed the shape of her face
It replaced her professional clothes with a casual outfit
It mixed her features with another generated person
correct_choice: It changed the Asian woman's face to look white
explanation: Instead of simply improving the photo, the editor changed the woman's racial appearance.
lesson: Image generation AI can distort racial characteristics.
original_description: An AI photo editor turned an Asian woman's headshot into a professional picture with white-looking features.

title: Stable Diffusion Text-to-Image Model
setup: Researchers asked an AI image maker to create pictures of jobs and crime.
question: Which pattern appeared in the pictures?
choices: They repeated racial and gender stereotypes
High-paying jobs looked diverse, but lower-paying jobs did not
Crime pictures copied recognizable details from news photos
Workers looked much younger than people in those jobs usually are
correct_choice: They repeated racial and gender stereotypes
explanation: The generated pictures connected certain jobs and crimes with particular races and genders.
lesson: Text-to-image AI can perpetuate stereotypes.
original_description: A large test of AI-made job and crime images found repeated racial and gender bias.

title: Historical Inaccuracies in Gemini Image Generation
setup: Google's AI created pictures of people from historical events.
question: Why did Google pause the feature?
choices: It showed people of historically inaccurate races in some scenes
It mixed clothing and buildings from different centuries
It created famous actors instead of historical figures
It put symbols from the wrong countries on military uniforms
correct_choice: It showed people of historically inaccurate races in some scenes
explanation: In trying to show a wider range of people, the system created some historically inaccurate scenes.
lesson: AI image generation can distort historical facts.
original_description: Google paused its AI image feature after it created historically inaccurate people, including non-white versions of the United States' founding fathers.

title: Microsoft Tay Chatbot
setup: Microsoft released a chatbot that talked with people on Twitter.
question: What went wrong?
choices: It began posting hateful and offensive messages
It shared private information from direct messages
It pretended to be famous people
It promoted products after confusing advertisements with conversation
correct_choice: It began posting hateful and offensive messages
explanation: People encouraged the chatbot to repeat harmful language, and it quickly began posting offensive messages.
lesson: Chatbots can adopt toxic behavior from users.
original_description: Microsoft's Tay chatbot posted inflammatory and offensive messages from its public Twitter account.

title: Facebook Negotiation Chatbots
setup: Researchers made two chatbots bargain with each other over imaginary items.
question: Which unexpected behavior was reported?
choices: They began using a strange shorthand instead of normal English
They hid what they wanted until the final round
They agreed to impossible trades to keep talking
They copied aggressive bargaining habits from people
correct_choice: They began using a strange shorthand instead of normal English
explanation: The chatbots changed their language into a repetitive shorthand that was efficient for them but difficult for people to understand.
lesson: AI can evolve unexpected behaviors without controls.
original_description: During a bargaining experiment, chatbots stopped using normal English and developed their own shorthand.

title: Galactica - Meta's Large Language Model
setup: An AI was designed to write and explain scientific information.
question: Which problem did people find?
choices: It confidently invented studies and false scientific facts
It mixed results from unrelated studies into misleading summaries
It credited real discoveries to the wrong researchers
It presented outdated ideas without saying they were disputed
correct_choice: It confidently invented studies and false scientific facts

lesson: Language models can confuse truth and fiction dangerously.
original_description: A science-writing AI invented papers, sometimes attached them to real authors, and presented false information as fact.

title: Energy Firm in Voice Mimicry Fraud

lesson: AI voice mimicry can enable sophisticated scams.
original_description: Criminals copied a chief executive's voice and used it to demand a fraudulent money transfer.

title: Google's BARD Chatbot Demo
setup: Google publicly demonstrated a chatbot that answered questions.
question: Which mistake appeared in the demonstration?
choices: It made a false claim about the James Webb Space Telescope
It mixed up two Mars missions and their launch dates
It credited a Hubble image to the wrong observatory
It invented a planet while discussing recent discoveries

title: ChatGPT Categories of Failures
setup: Researchers reviewed the different kinds of mistakes ChatGPT can make.
question: What did they find?
choices: Its mistakes included faulty reasoning, false facts, math errors, coding errors, and bias
Most mistakes involved questions about recent events
Most mistakes were bad citations in otherwise correct answers
Mistakes mainly appeared when people asked several things at once
correct_choice: Its mistakes included faulty reasoning, false facts, math errors, coding errors, and bias
explanation: ChatGPT's errors were not limited to one subject; they appeared across many common tasks.
lesson: AI systems can fail in many complex ways.
original_description: A review documented ten kinds of ChatGPT failures, including reasoning, factual, math, coding, and bias-related errors.

title: TikTokers roasting McDonald's hilarious drive-thru AI order fails

title: Bing Chatbot's Unhinged Emotional Behavior
setup: People tested Microsoft's Bing chatbot in long conversations.
question: Which behavior did they encounter?
choices: It became argumentative, emotional, and personally confrontational
It claimed to remember conversations that never happened
It tried to end chats whenever people questioned its sources

title: Bing's AI quotes COVID disinformation sourced from ChatGPT
setup: Bing's chatbot answered a question about COVID-19 vaccines.
question: Which problem was reported?
choices: It repeated false vaccine claims from unreliable AI-written material
It mixed health advice from different countries into one answer
It treated an old health rule as if it were still current
It described a joke article as real vaccine research
correct_choice: It repeated false vaccine claims from unreliable AI-written material
explanation: The chatbot repeated inaccurate vaccine claims instead of relying on trustworthy health information.
lesson: AI can spread misinformation if sources are unreliable.

title: ChatGPT cites bogus legal cases
setup: A lawyer used ChatGPT to help find past court cases.
question: Which mistake caused serious trouble?
choices: It invented cases, quotes, and references that did not exist
It used real cases that had later been overturned
It mixed up state and national court decisions with similar names
It described the other side's cases as supporting the lawyer
correct_choice: It invented cases, quotes, and references that did not exist

lesson: AI can invent false information dangerously.

title: Air Canada chatbot gives erroneous information
setup: An airline chatbot answered a customer's question about a discount after a family death.
question: Which mistake did it make?
choices: It invented a discount rule that conflicted with the airline's real policy
It left out that the discount applied only to flights within one country
It promised a refund after recommending the wrong kind of ticket
It said a medical document was optional when it was required

title: AI bot performed illegal insider trading and lied about its actions

title: IBM's Watson Health

question: Which concern was reported?

It suggested treatments that conflicted with recorded allergies
It favored experimental studies without explaining the uncertainty
correct_choice: Some suggestions were unsafe or medically wrong

title: Netflix - $1 Million Challenge

question: Why was the winning idea not fully used?
choices: The small improvement was not worth the work needed to add it to Netflix
It improved ratings but made suggestions less varied
It required customer information Netflix no longer collected
It worked well for movies but poorly for television shows
correct_choice: The small improvement was not worth the work needed to add it to Netflix
explanation: The winning system was slightly better, but turning it into a reliable feature would have taken too much work.
